title: Memories From Below the Grape Trellis
synopsis: A story of the relationship between a child and a grandpa.

fullText.simplified:
葡萄架下的回忆

    每年6月，很多人也许会忆起高考。可是我，总会想起我的外公。
    我是外公外婆带大的。听妈妈说，我小的时候，特别爱哭，特别是睡觉的时候。外婆好不容易哄我入睡，外公“吧嗒吧嗒”的脚步声，一下子就可以把我从梦中惊醒，醒来后我总是哭。外公因为这个，没少挨外婆骂。可即便是这样，外公还是很爱我。
    记忆中，外公总是搬来凳子，抱着我，在家里的葡萄架下，一边扇着扇子，一边给我讲故事。郁郁葱葱的葡萄叶，把葡萄架遮得严严实实的。阳光照在葡萄架上，只能透过几缕金光，照在地上，亮晶晶的，漂亮极了。那时候，我总是缠着外公问：“外公外公，我什么时候才可以吃葡萄呀？”外公总会轻轻地刮一下我的鼻子，“小馋猫，那要等到秋天。”“可我现在就想吃，外公给我摘嘛”……最后外公总是拗不过我，为我摘下还没熟的小葡萄。青色的葡萄，甜中带涩……
    可是小时候，我并不太喜欢外公。那时候，我特别喜欢一个人玩过家家。我喜欢把家里所有大大小小的凳子都搬到门口，组合起来，为自己建造一个大“城堡”，葡萄架下的空地，就是我的舞厅；几张凳子组合成我的卧室、厨房和餐厅。我喜欢在那小小的地方，做着我大大的公主梦。外公工作，总要经过我用凳子堵着的门口，每次经过，他都不得不把凳子全部搬走。我怪他打乱了我建造的“城堡”，打扰了我的公主梦。他怪我总是搬凳子堵着门口，让他出入不方便。我俩相持不下时，我总哭着说：“我讨厌你。以后等我赚了钱，我要养外婆，养爸爸妈妈，养叔叔阿姨，养表哥表姐……养所有的人，就是不养你！”每当我说这句话的时候，外公总是叹了口气，一边帮我摆回凳子，一边无奈地说：“唉！我等不到你养我的时候咯！”那时候，我并不知道外公说这句话的含义，只知道只要我说这句话，外公就会妥协。所以，这句话，我说了无数遍……
    长大后，我和爸爸妈妈搬到城里，不和外公外婆住一块儿了。但是外公还是会时不时地来城里照顾我。亲戚聚会时，舅舅总会开我玩笑，说起我小时候生气时说的“不养外公”的话，外公总是在一旁看着我，不说话，憨憨地笑。长大后的我，当然知道那句话是不对的，也明白了外公说的“等不到”的意思，我多想向外公说一句，“小时候不懂事，对不起。我希望我能尽我所能地养你，和你在一起”。但是那时叛逆期的我，硬是倔强着没说一句话。
（未完待续）
fullText.traditional:
葡萄架下的回憶

    每年6月，很多人也許會憶起高考。可是我，總會想起我的外公。
    我是外公外婆帶大的。聽媽媽說，我小的時候，特別愛哭，特別是睡覺的時候。外婆好不容易哄我入睡，外公“吧嗒吧嗒”的腳步聲，一下子就可以把我從夢中驚醒，醒來後我總是哭。外公因為這個，沒少挨外婆罵。可即便是這樣，外公還是很愛我。
    記憶中，外公總是搬來凳子，抱著我，在家裡的葡萄架下，一邊扇著扇子，一邊給我講故事。鬱鬱蔥蔥的葡萄葉，把葡萄架遮得嚴嚴實實的。陽光照在葡萄架上，只能透過幾縷金光，照在地上，亮晶晶的，漂亮極了。那時候，我總是纏著外公問：“外公外公，我什麼時候才可以吃葡萄呀？”外公總會輕輕地刮一下我的鼻子，“小饞貓，那要等到秋天。”“可我現在就想吃，外公給我摘嘛”……最後外公總是拗不過我，為我摘下還沒熟的小葡萄。青色的葡萄，甜中帶澀……
    可是小時候，我並不太喜歡外公。那時候，我特別喜歡一個人玩過家家。我喜歡把家裡所有大大小小的凳子都搬到門口，組合起來，為自己建造一個大“城堡”，葡萄架下的空地，就是我的舞廳；幾張凳子組合成我的臥室、廚房和餐廳。我喜歡在那小小的地方，做著我大大的公主夢。外公工作，總要經過我用凳子堵著的門口，每次經過，他都不得不把凳子全部搬走。我怪他打亂了我建造的“城堡”，打擾了我的公主夢。他怪我總是搬凳子堵著門口，讓他出入不方便。我倆相持不下時，我總哭著說：“我討厭你。以後等我賺了錢，我要養外婆，養爸爸媽媽，養叔叔阿姨，養表哥表姐……養所有的人，就是不養你！”每當我說這句話的時候，外公總是嘆了口氣，一邊幫我擺回凳子，一邊無奈地說：“唉！我等不到你養我的時候咯！”那時候，我並不知道外公說這句話的含義，只知道只要我說這句話，外公就會妥協。所以，這句話，我說了無數遍……
    長大後，我和爸爸媽媽搬到城裡，不和外公外婆住一塊兒了。但是外公還是會時不時地來城裡照顧我。親戚聚會時，舅舅總會開我玩笑，說起我小時候生氣時說的“不養外公”的話，外公總是在一旁看著我，不說話，憨憨地笑。長大後的我，當然知道那句話是不對的，也明白了外公說的“等不到”的意思，我多想向外公說一句，“小時候不懂事，對不起。我希望我能盡我所能地養你，和你在一起”。但是那時叛逆期的我，硬是倔強著沒說一句話。
（未完待續）

sentences.traditional: 只知道只要我說這句話，外公就會妥協。
sentences.pinyin: zhǐ zhī dào zhǐ yào wǒ shuō zhè jù huà wài gōng jiù huì tuǒ xié
sentences.english: At the time, I didn’t understand the meaning of grandpa’s words.

sentences.simplified: 所以，这句话，我说了无数遍……
sentences.traditional: 所以，這句話，我說了無數遍……
sentences.pinyin: suǒ yǐ zhè jù huà wǒ shuō le wú shù biàn
sentences.english: I only knew that whenever I said this phrase, grandpa would give in.
Therefore, I said this phrase uncountable times…

sentences.simplified: 长大后，我和爸爸妈妈搬到城里，不和外公外婆住一块儿了。
sentences.traditional: 長大後，我和爸爸媽媽搬到城裡，不和外公外婆住一塊兒了。
sentences.pinyin: zhǎng dà hòu wǒ hé bà ba mā ma bān dào chéng lǐ bù hé wài gōng wài pó zhù yí kuài'r le

sentences.simplified: 但是外公还是会时不时地来城里照顾我。
sentences.traditional: 但是外公還是會時不時地來城裡照顧我。
sentences.pinyin: dàn shì wài gōng hái shì huì shí bù shí de lái chéng lǐ zhào gù wǒ
sentences.english: After I grew up, my parents and I moved into the city, and didn’t live with grandpa and grandma anymore.

sentences.simplified: 亲戚聚会时，舅舅总会开我玩笑，
sentences.traditional: 親戚聚會時，舅舅總會開我玩笑，
sentences.pinyin: qīn qi jù huì shí jiù jiu zǒng huì kāi wǒ wán xiào
sentences.english: But grandpa would still come to the city to look after me from time to time.

sentences.simplified: 说起我小时候生气时说的“不养外公”的话，
sentences.traditional: 說起我小時候生氣時說的“不養外公”的話，
sentences.pinyin: shuō qǐ wǒ xiǎo shí hou shēng qì shí shuō de bù yǎng wài gōng de huà
sentences.english: At family gatherings, my uncle would always joke with me ..

sentences.simplified: 外公总是在一旁看着我，不说话，憨憨地笑。
sentences.traditional: 外公總是在一旁看著我，不說話，憨憨地笑。
sentences.pinyin: wài gōng zǒng shì zài yì páng kàn zhe wǒ bù shuō huà hān hān de xiào
sentences.english: .. by mentioning how when I was little I would get angry and say “I won’t take care of grandpa”.

sentences.simplified: 长大后的我，当然知道那句话是不对的，
sentences.traditional: 長大後的我，當然知道那句話是不對的，
sentences.pinyin: zhǎng dà hòu de wǒ dāng rán zhī dào nà jù huà shì bú duì de
sentences.english: Grandpa would always sit by the side looking at me in silence with a silly smile.

sentences.simplified: 也明白了外公说的“等不到”的意思，
sentences.traditional: 也明白了外公說的“等不到”的意思，
sentences.pinyin: yě míng bai le wài gōng shuō de děng bu dào de yì si
sentences.english: After growing up, I of course understood that saying these things was not right.

sentences.simplified: 我多想向外公说一句，“小时候不懂事，对不起。
sentences.traditional: 我多想向外公說一句，“小時候不懂事，對不起。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ duō xiǎng xiàng wài gōng shuō yí jù xiǎo shí hou bù dǒng shì duì bu qǐ
sentences.english: I also understood what grandpa meant when he said he “won’t be able to wait”.

sentences.simplified: 我希望我能尽我所能地养你，和你在一起”。
sentences.traditional: 我希望我能盡我所能地養你，和你在一起”。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ xī wàng wǒ néng jìn wǒ suǒ néng de yǎng nǐ hé nǐ zài yì qǐ
sentences.english: I often wanted to tell grandpa: “I didn’t know better when I was little. I’m sorry.”

sentences.simplified: 但是那时叛逆期的我，硬是倔强着没说一句话。
sentences.traditional: 但是那時叛逆期的我，硬是倔強著沒說一句話。
sentences.pinyin: dàn shì nà shí pàn nì qī de wǒ yìng shì jué jiàng zhe méi shuō yí jù huà
sentences.english: “I wish I could take care of you to my utmost ability, and be together with you.”
But being in a rebellious phase, I obstinately never said anything.

sentences.traditional: （未完待續）

sentence_translations: Memories From Below the Grape Trellis
Each year in June, a lot of people will perhaps remember the college entrance exam.
But for me, I will always think of my grandpa.
I was raised by my grandma and grandpa.
My mom told me that I often cried when I was little, and especially when it was time to sleep.
After my grandma had finally soothed me to sleep, ..
.. the tapping sound of grandpa’s footsteps could quickly wake me up from my dreams.
After waking up, I would always cry.
Due to this, my grandpa would often get scolded by grandma.
Despite this, my grandpa still loved me deeply.
I remember that grandpa would always bring out a stool and hold me ..
.. fanning me while telling me stories under the grape trellis in the house.
The lush grape leaves closely covered the grape trellis.
The sunlight shone on top of the grape trellis, and only a few strands of golden light passed through ..
.. glisteringly lighting up the floor, looking extremely beautiful.
Back then, I would often bother grandpa asking: “Grandpa, grandpa, when can I eat the grapes?”
Grandpa would always gently tap my nose: “Greedy little cat. You have to wait until autumn.”
“But I want to eat them now. Pick one for me, grandpa…”
Finally, grandpa would always capitulate and pick a not yet ripe grape for me.
A green grape, with a tart flavor within the sweet…
However, when I was little, I didn’t like my grandpa very much.
At the time, I especially liked to play house alone.
I liked to grab all the big and small stools in the house and move them to the entrance.
I would combine them together, to build a big “castle” for myself.
The vacant space below the grape trellis became my ballroom.
A few stools assembled together became my bedroom, kitchen and dining room.
I liked to sit in that tiny, tiny space, dreaming my big, big princess dreams.
Grandpa was working, and would always pass through the entrance I had blocked up with stools.
Whenever he passed, he had to move all the stools away.
I blamed him for disrupting the “castle” I had built, and for disturbing my princess dreams.
He blamed me for always blocking the entrance with stools, making it difficult for him to enter and exit.
When the two of us came to a stalemate, I would always cry saying:
“I hate you. Later when I make money I will take care of grandma, dad, mom, uncle, aunt and my cousins…”
“I will take care of everyone except for you!”
Whenever I said this, grandpa would always sigh, and help me put the stools back while reluctantly saying:
“Sigh! I won’t be able to wait until you can take care of me.”
At the time, I didn’t understand the meaning of grandpa’s words.
I only knew that whenever I said this phrase, grandpa would give in.
Therefore, I said this phrase uncountable times…
After I grew up, my parents and I moved into the city, and didn’t live with grandpa and grandma anymore.
But grandpa would still come to the city to look after me from time to time.
At family gatherings, my uncle would always joke with me ..
.. by mentioning how when I was little I would get angry and say “I won’t take care of grandpa”.
Grandpa would always sit by the side looking at me in silence with a silly smile.
After growing up, I of course understood that saying these things was not right.
I also understood what grandpa meant when he said he “won’t be able to wait”.
I often wanted to tell grandpa: “I didn’t know better when I was little. I’m sorry.”
“I wish I could take care of you to my utmost ability, and be together with you.”
But being in a rebellious phase, I obstinately never said anything.
(To be continued)
